cands.name: David Pan

money.note: Individuals gave $92,086; PAC money $2,250; candidate's own money $9,000. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Professor of German at UC Irvine since 2006. Earlier taught at Washington University in St. Louis, Stanford and Penn State. Worked as a management consultant at McKinsey in Los Angeles, edited the journal Telos, and served on the State Department's Commission on Unalienable Rights (2019-2020). Republican candidate for CA-46 in 2024 and 2026.

endorsements.text: Endorsed in 2026 by the California Republican Party, the Orange County Republican Party, the California Republican Assembly and Reform California, among other groups and voter guides.

cands.gaps: We found no record of David Pan's positions on data centers, development or growth, property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, guns, abortion or teacher pay. He has not held office, so there is no record of official actions. The campaign site gives his stated views on border security but not on specific immigration enforcement measures or H-1B visas. His pledge to end lobbying influence is a constitutional amendment proposal, not a pledge about refusing contributions. The campaign issues page was cut off partway through, so any later text on it was not read. We could not find his birth year or when he first moved to California. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in either 2024 or 2026.

cands.bio: Democrat representing California's 46th District in the U.S. House since 2017. Former investment banker, real estate broker, attorney and college instructor. Served in the California Assembly (1998–2004), Orange County Board of Supervisors (2004–2006) and California Senate (2006–2014).

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, the California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), the National Union of Healthcare Workers, Equality California, the Sierra Club Angeles Chapter and Planned Parenthood of Orange and San Bernardino Counties' Community Action Fund.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions by Correa on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land protection, police pay, gun laws or school choice. He did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026, so there is no self-reported platform on those pages. The sources do not say when his family returned from Mexico to California beyond "five years later" after age two. No controversies or foreign ties were documented in the pages reviewed. The Ballotpedia page was cut off partway through the 117th Congress key votes, so older votes were not read.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.
